newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comment on ING 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comment on ING 1996 results.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) on Thursday reported a 25.4 percent increase in 1996 net profit to 3.32 billion guilders.
The company said it was confident about the outlook for 1997 but that it was too early to make a profit forecast.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on ING's results:

TOM BENNETT, PARIBAS: "The thing that stands out is the dividend which is up 20 percent. We were going for a (net profit) of around 3.15 (billion guilders) which was too cautious. It looks like they had a very strong fourth quarter on the insurance side, although it's not yet clear why. As usual they have made a relatively cautious comment in the first quarter. They do say they are confident...We had it as a buy and it's clearly very attractive. It has a long history of solid earnings growth and that's in a hard currency, guilders."

HEINI HAKKER, BZW: "These figures are very good. It's their strongest profit growth ever...There's healthy profit growth in all activities...Over the whole year, ING put aside 530 million guilders related to the launch of the euro, compared with provisions of just 275 million in the first nine months...The 2.55 billion guilders of hidden reserves are broadly as expected...The absence of a clear profit forecast can be attributed to ING's usual caution, but with so much money put aside in provisions, there's quite a lot of room for 1997. I am maintaining my Buy recommendation and I might raise my earnings per share estimates somewhat after tomorrow's analysts' meeting."
